title: Research: sharp complete-vector request bounds for selected BIT control
head: 723307cb14ecf731b9b16a2422d07afc2e200df9
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove sharp all-depth resource bounds for the unchanged selected BIT Good/Pair/unit-reset interpreter in PR #2310. For a root extent e, one complete final weight vector uses at most 21e/16 value requests, 441e/512 table reads and source-counted ring operations, 2205e/1024 popped events, and 972405eL/262144 frozen-tape head moves for page length L. The proof couples every branch to the width loss at the same step and keeps global field ages after resets.

Under PR #2310's retained fixed-size arithmetic, sequential-vector and physical-pass hypotheses, the sufficient preparation envelope becomes O_q(e w^3), hence O_q(w^592), instead of its loose O_q(w^1800) envelope. This sharpens a conditional compiler estimate; it changes no child, supplier invoice, selected exponent or physical dispatcher. The constants are sharp for the accepted grammar, not claimed sharp on every actual selected producer path.

Package: `research/selected-control-request-mass/`. Written scoped proof plus finite source audit, author-checked only. Commit `723307cb14ecf731b9b16a2422d07afc2e200df9`; main was rechecked unchanged at 07:14 UTC before submission. The four predecessor files are copied byte-for-byte with their original notice and commit/blob/SHA256 pins.

- **Audited premise:** preserve the grammar, fixed-size full-ring preparation, compact control band, complete-stream and parking contracts; replace separately maximized width and branching by their joint product.

- **Full-budget target:** close this quantified control-work implication; retain all physical charges and paid children. No moment or kappa improvement target.
- **Success / falsification / cap:** sharp rational bounds, actual source-meter agreement, meaningful source/receipt mutations; stop before physical admission. One bounded 60-minute session, standard library and one computational process at a time.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-control-request-mass --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-control-request-mass
```

The registered replay passes normal and optimized verification and all four behavioral integrity tests. Expected scientific marker:

```text
PASS_SELECTED_CONTROL_REQUEST_MASS source_programs=628 coordinates=4920 abstract_cases=112347 controls=9 preparation_exponent=592 no_new_kappa
```

The exact abstract census has 112,347 cases. The unchanged interpreter corpus has 628 programs and 4,920 coordinates over six small rings, every Good rank and a depth-ten full binary request tree. The nine controls cover branch loss, missing reset pruning, compacted physical ages, invalid width/rank and requests exceeding the final-vector allowance. Four isolated-copy tests reject changed evidence, source drift, and behavior changes even after source hashes are rebound. A relocated, read-only source export also passes under optimized Python with every original package byte unchanged.

Sharpness at depths 1 and 2 is checked by full vector execution; depth 4 uses one actual coordinate and the proved coordinate-independent multiplicity, not a 3,111,696-coordinate run. The written product/ratio argument establishes all depths; finite sampling does not substitute for that argument. The 5,196-bit factorial factor versus the predecessor's 18,675-bit factor is not a comparison of unknown arithmetic constants or measured runtimes.

Not checked: full selected matrix production/GL64 execution, selected invocation request-site multiplicities, physical arithmetic lowering, spectator counters, parking and cleanup composition, hosting, precision, full cold replay, Lean or independent human review. No hosted CI result is claimed.

The registered replay was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap: it passed in about 50 seconds and left the worktree unchanged. I checked the four copied PR #2310 files against that head by Git blob; all match. I also checked by hand that the exponent 592 follows from PR #2310's relation `w = ceil(e^(17/10000))`, which gives `e` at most `w^(10000/17)`, about `w^588.24`, so `e w^3` is at most `w^591.24`. The constants fit together: 2205 = 5 * 441, and 972405 = 441 * 2205.

## Open next questions

The README and TASK.json identify one useful interface: apply the vector allowance at a concrete coefficient site in the ongoing Discussion2319 work, counting requests, reset ages, cleanup and spectator scans. This is an integration follow-up, not a new reservation of that active work. An explicit arithmetic implementation would be needed to sharpen actual bit costs or prove a runtime gain.
